What CTET Paper 2 asks on Ratio and Proportion

Questions cover ratio in simplest form, proportion, the unitary method, percentage, and direct and inverse variation, usually as short word problems.

Key facts & formulas to remember

  • A ratio compares like quantities and has no unit; write it in simplest form.
  • If a : b = c : d then a × d = b × c (product of extremes = product of means).
  • Unitary method: find the value of one unit, then multiply.
  • x% means x/100; multiply a fraction or ratio by 100 to get a percentage.
  • Direct variation: more ⇒ more; inverse variation: more ⇒ less (e.g. speed and time).

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Leaving a ratio unsimplified.
  • Comparing quantities in different units without converting first.
  • Treating an inverse-variation problem as direct.

quiz.title: CTET Ratio and Proportion Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper II–pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: CTET Paper 2 Maths: Ratio and Proportion

questions.q: If A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 8 : 9, then A : C is equal to:
questions.explanation: Given A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 8 : 9. To find A : C, we can multiply the two ratios: (A / B) × (B / C) = (3 / 4) × (8 / 9) = 24 / 36 = 2 / 3. Therefore, A : C = 2 : 3.
To convert a decimal into a percentage, multiply it by 100 and add the percentage sign (%): 0.05 × 100% = 5%.

questions.q: If 15 pens cost ₹225, find the cost of 8 such pens using the unitary method.
questions.explanation: Cost of 15 pens = ₹225. Cost of 1 pen = 225 / 15 = ₹15. Cost of 8 pens = 15 × 8 = ₹120.

questions.q: What is the simple interest on ₹4000 at a rate of 5% per annum for 3 years?
An article marked at ₹800 is sold for ₹680. Find the discount percentage.
questions.explanation: Marked Price (MP) = ₹800, Selling Price (SP) = ₹680. Discount = MP - SP = 800 - 680 = ₹120. Discount % = (Discount / MP) × 100 = (120 / 800) × 100 = 15%.

questions.q: If the price of petrol increases by 25%, by what percentage must a car owner reduce the consumption of petrol so that the expenditure on petrol remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: Let initial price be ₹100 and consumption be 100 units. Total expenditure = ₹10,000. New price = ₹125. To keep expenditure at ₹10,000, new consumption = 10000 / 125 = 80 units. Reduction in consumption = 100 - 80 = 20 units, which is a 20% reduction.

questions.q: A sum of money becomes double of itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many times will it become 4 times itself at the same rate of interest?
questions.explanation: Let Principal = P. In 8 years, interest earned is P (since amount becomes 2P). So, interest in 8 years = P. To become 4 times, the total interest needed is 3P. Since P interest takes 8 years, 3P interest will take 8 × 3 = 24 years.

questions.q: If 12 men or 18 women can reap a field in 14 days, in how many days can 8 men and 16 women reap the same field?
questions.explanation: Given 12 men = 18 women, so 1 man = 18 / 12 = 1.5 women. Convert 8 men into women equivalents: 8 men = 8 × 1.5 = 12 women. Total women = 12 + 16 = 28 women. Using inverse proportion: 18 women × 14 days = 28 women × D2 \implies D2 = (18 × 14) / 28 = 9 days.

questions.q: A shopkeeper allows a successive discount of 20% and 10% on an article. If the article is sold for ₹504, find its marked price.
questions.explanation: Let Marked Price be MP. Selling Price = MP × (1 - 20/100) × (1 - 10/100) = MP × (80/100) × (90/100) = MP × 0.72. Given SP = 504. So, 0.72 × MP = 504 \implies MP = 504 / 0.72 = ₹700.

questions.q: The ratio of copper and zinc in an alloy is 9 : 4. If the weight of zinc in the alloy is 24 kg, find the total weight of the alloy.
questions.explanation: Let copper be 9x and zinc be 4x. Given 4x = 24 \implies x = 6. Total weight of the alloy = 9x + 4x = 13x = 13 × 6 = 78 kg.

faq.q: How do you check if four numbers are in proportion?
faq.a: They are in proportion if the product of the extremes equals the product of the means (a × d = b × c).
You first find the value of a single unit, then scale up or down. It is the backbone of most ratio and percentage word problems.
